audit_items.proof_trace: The code accepts data column sidecars in any order without validating the required (slot, column_index) ordering. DataColumnsByRangeRequestItems::add checks slot range, column index validity, inclusion proof, and duplicates, but never verifies that incoming sidecars maintain ascending order. Subsequent HashMap-based grouping in responses_with_custody_columns further destroys ordering.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker sends data_column_sidecars_by_range responses out of order (e.g., slot 103 before slot 100). All sidecars pass validation and are accepted, violating the spec MUST requirement. While Lighthouse buffers all responses and groups by block_root (mitigating direct exploitation), this violates protocol compliance and could enable resource exhaustion if ordering was intended for early termination.
